chunks: And Ṣafwān narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, who said:

I asked Abā Ibrāhīm عليه السلام about a man who had a woman with him, and she arrived in Makkah while she was not praying. She did not become pure until the Day of Tarwiyah, then she became pure and performed tawaf of the House, but she did not perform saʿy between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah until she departed to ʿArafāt. Should she count that tawaf, or repeat it before al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah?
He عليه السلام said: "She counts that first tawaf and builds upon it."

key_terms.تَبْنِي عَلَيْهِ: she continues and builds upon it without repeating from the beginning
key_terms.تَسْعَ: to perform saʿy between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah
key_terms.طَافَتْ بِالْبَيْتِ: she performed tawaf around the Kaʿbah
key_terms.لَا تُصَلِّي: not performing salat (prayer), referring here to menstruation preventing prayer
key_terms.يَوْمَ التَّرْوِيَةِ: the Day of Tarwiyah, the eighth of Dhū al-Ḥijjah in the hajj rites

ai.seo_question: If a menstruating woman performs tawaf after becoming pure but goes to ʿArafāt before saʿy, does she need to repeat the tawaf?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a menstruating woman in hajj who became pure on the Day of Tarwiyah, performed tawaf, and then left for ʿArafāt before completing the saʿy. Imam Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام rules that her first tawaf remains valid and that she should continue on its basis rather than repeat it.
